overview: Order is an experimentally determined value from the rate law; molecularity is a theoretical count of colliding species in a single elementary step.
genZNote: Order is what the lab data says. Molecularity is what theory says about one elementary step.

aspects.label: How Determined
aspects.valueA: Found experimentally from rate data (never assumed from the equation).
aspects.valueB: Deduced theoretically from the proposed elementary reaction mechanism.

aspects.label: Possible Values
aspects.valueA: Can be zero, a fraction, or any positive number.
aspects.valueB: Always a whole positive number (1, 2, rarely 3).

aspects.label: Applies To
aspects.valueB: Only a single elementary step, never a complex multi-step reaction as a whole.
